'''Charles Aaron''' "'''Bubba'''" '''Smith''' (February 28, 1945 – August 3, 2011) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] and actor. Smith played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Baltimore Colts]], [[Oakland Raiders]], and [[Houston Oilers]], and [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]

Smith played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]], where he twice earned [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. Smith had a major role in a [[1966 Notre Dame vs. Michigan State football game|10–10 tie]] against [[1966 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|Notre Dame]] in 1966 that was billed as "[[Game of the Century (college football)|The Game of the Century]]". He is one of only six players to have his jersey number retired by the program. He was inducted into the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 1988.<ref name="msuftblobit2">{{cite web|title=Former Two-Time All-American Bubba Smith Passes Away At Age 66|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/080311aaa.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150112233640/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/080311aaa.html|archive-date=January 12, 2015|access-date=January 20, 2015|work=msuspartans.com}}</ref>

The [[List of first overall National Football League Draft picks|first overall pick]] of the [[1967 NFL/AFL draft]], Smith played nine years in the NFL for the Colts, Raiders, and Oilers from 1967 to 1976. He was the Colts' starting left defensive end for five seasons, playing in [[Super Bowl]]s [[Super Bowl III|III]] and [[Super Bowl V|V]]. He was named to two [[Pro Bowl]]s and was a first-team [[All-Pro]] in 1971.<ref name="cdabebmtent2">{{cite news|date=August 4, 2011|title=Local football legend Bubba Smith dies at 66|url=http://www.beaumontenterprise.com/sports/article/Local-football-legend-Bubba-Smith-dies-at-66-1718871.php|access-date=January 20, 2015|work=Beaumont Enterprise|last1=Dabe|first1=Christopher|archive-date=April 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230429144430/https://www.beaumontenterprise.com/sports/article/Local-football-legend-Bubba-Smith-dies-at-66-1718871.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> He had tremendous quickness despite being {{height|ft=6|in=7}} and {{convert|265|lb}},<ref name="bsmithpfrcom2">{{cite web|title=Bubba Smith|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitBu00.htm|access-date=January 20, 2015|work=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> a combination which usually earned him a [[double-team]].<ref name="cdabebmtent2" />

During his acting career, Smith specialized in comedic roles in film, television, and television advertising. For about a decade following his retirement from football, he appeared in various commercials for [[Miller Lite]], alongside Chicago Bears linebacker [[Dick Butkus]]. His best-known role was as [[Moses Hightower (character)|Moses Hightower]] in the first six ''[[Police Academy (franchise)|Police Academy]]'' movies.<ref name="cnolandlat2">{{Cite web |last=Noland |first=Claire |date=August 4, 2011 |title=Bubba Smith obituary: NFL player turned beer pitchman dies at 66 |url=https://www.latimes.com/news/obituaries/la-me-bubba-smith-20110804,0,1560282.story |access-date=January 20, 2015 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref>

Smith was posthumously diagnosed with [[chronic traumatic encephalopathy]], a neurological condition generally related to head trauma. He is one of at least 345 [[List of NFL players with chronic traumatic encephalopathy|NFL players to be diagnosed after death]] with this disease.<ref>{{cite web |title=Researchers Find CTE in 345 of 376 Former NFL Players Studied |url=https://www.bumc.bu.edu/busm/2023/02/06/researchers-find-cte-in-345-of-376-former-nfl-players-studied/ |website= Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine |access-date=March 26, 2023}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]]. He was a member of three 49ers teams that won the [[Super Bowl]]. '''George Jessel''' "'''Buddy'''" '''Curry''' (born June 4, 1958) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for eight seasons from 1980 to 1987. He played [[college football]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. '''William Eldridge''' "'''Bucky'''" '''Brooks Jr.''' (born January 22, 1971) is an American [[sportswriter]] and former professional [[American football|football]] player.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=BROOKBUC01 |title=Bucky Brooks |access-date=September 19, 2008 |publisher=databasefootball.com |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100218125101/http://databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=BROOKBUC01 |archive-date=February 18, 2010 }}</ref> He played for five [[National Football League]] (NFL) teams in a five-year career, primarily as a [[kick returner]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bucky Brooks Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrooBu20.htm |access-date=2024-06-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was drafted in the second round of the [[1994 NFL draft]] by the Buffalo Bills with the 48th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1994 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1994/draft.htm |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Brooks is in his sixth season as an analyst for [[NFL Network]] and [[NFL.com]]. He contributes weekly columns, as well as video features including "Scout’s Take" and "On the Beat" on NFL.com, and offers interactive analysis on the latest NFL topics and headlines with weekly live online chats. For the 2010 season, Brooks returned as an analyst for ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'', NFL.com's in-game coverage of the Network's eight live, regular season game broadcasts. NFL.com/LIVE: Thursday Night Football presents a live show throughout the game including “live look ins” of the game, reports from the field and highlights.
